raw_response:
I’m getting old, so I don’t like to toss money around on fancy ideas. On my 5 mu I still plant cotton, same as before. I’ve farmed this land many years, and for cotton here the main thing is to get it in on time, give enough fertilizer early, and watch the field after emergence. If I spend too little, the plants stay weak and the bolls are not good. But if I spend too much, that is cash tied up, and with only 5 mu I have to keep the cost steady. I have a well, so if spring is dry I can water, but pumping costs money, so I won’t irrigate unless the soil is really short of moisture. I usually use improved seed from the local market, not the most expensive one, just the kind people around here say is stable. Fertilizer, I’ll put most at the start and then add a little later if the plants look like they need strength. Pesticide I won’t spray blindly. If I see aphids or bollworm pressure, or too many weeds early, then I use what is available in town. At my age, family labor still matters, and if picking time gets tight, we may hire a little help.
